deep.reconstruction:
Context: in E477 Euler studies the double sums later called Euler sums or double zeta values. In his notation ∫1/z^μ (1/y^ν) = Σ_{z} z^{-μ} Σ_{y<z} y^{-ν}, which is ζ(μ,ν) in the strict-inequality convention, and ∫1/z^m = ζ(m). His 'second method' takes the partial-fraction decomposition of 1/(x^m (x±d)^n) and sums over x and d. This gives ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) (or the corresponding product expression) as a combination of products ζ(m+k)ζ(n−k) and double sums ζ(m+k, n−k).

The previous page split the result into a 'pars prima' and a 'pars altera', with alternating factors (1±1) and (1∓1). This page writes out the collapsed forms according to the parity of m and of n.

Pars prima, m even:
2 Σ_{k even} C(m+k−1,k) ζ(m+k)ζ(n−k) − Σ_{k≥0} C(m+k−1,k) ζ(m+k, n−k).

Pars prima, m odd:
−2 Σ_{k odd} C(m+k−1,k) ζ(m+k)ζ(n−k) + Σ_{k≥0} C(m+k−1,k) ζ(m+k, n−k).

Pars posterior: the same two formulas with m and n interchanged.

The sums stop when n−k (or m−k) reaches 0. Terms with ζ(1) are divergent and must cancel. Euler says this on the next page: 'hoc infinitum ex calculo egredi debet' (this infinity must drop out of the calculation).

This is the derivation of Euler's decomposition formula, which expresses a product ζ(m)ζ(n) through double zeta values with binomial coefficients. The next page combines it with the 'first method' reflection theorem ζ(m,n)+ζ(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n), in Euler's convention. He then classifies everything by weight m+n ('ordines') and evaluates the double sums weight by weight.
errors: Misprint in 'Pars posterior si n sit numerus impar', second term. The print has ∫1/z^{n+3} (1/z^{m−3}; it should be the product ∫1/z^{n+3}·∫1/z^{m−3}. The coefficient 2n(n+1)(n+2)/1·2·3 and the matching m-odd formula confirm a product term.
Heading misprint: 'Pro posterior' should read 'Pars posterior'.
The formulas are formal. Terms involving ∫1/z (the harmonic series) diverge and cancel only in combination; Euler acknowledges this on the next page.
On the previous page, the (m+1)(m+2)/1·2·3 coefficient lacks the factor m (it should be m(m+1)(m+2)/1·2·3). That page's last line is also uncertain in the transcription.

ideas.what: Parity-collapsed partial-fraction identity expressing products ζ(m+k)ζ(n−k) and double sums ζ(m+k,n−k) with binomial coefficients C(m+k−1,k); the weight m+n is preserved
ideas.modern_name: Euler's decomposition formula / double shuffle relations for double zeta values
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477, 1775/76); revived by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995), Zagier, Gangl–Kaneko–Zagier (2006)
ideas.where_published: E477, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 20 (1776); Opera Omnia I.15

ideas.what: Observation (stated on the next page) that all double sums occurring have constant total exponent μ+ν = m+n, and organization of the work by this sum
ideas.modern_name: weight grading of multiple zeta values
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477); the modern formalism is due to Zagier and Hoffman

ideas.what: Formal cancellation of divergent ζ(1) terms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier (2006), with an informal precursor in Euler

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known derivation of Euler's decomposition formula for double zeta values. It is extensively cited in the modern multiple zeta value literature, and nothing on the page appears unrecognized.
transcription_corrections: 'Pro poſterior ſi n ſit numerus par' — the print does read 'Pro'; it is a typographical error for 'Pars'.
In 'Pars poſterior ſi n ſit numerus impar', the transcription correctly shows the printed '(1/z^{m−3}', but the intended form is '·∫1/z^{m−3}'.
In the first block, the third product term is printed without the multiplication dot: ∫1/z^{m+4} ∫1/z^{n−4} + etc.; the transcription matches.
